label: <DEL> in short sequences, or y/s/v/l input mid-original-phase
explanation: Never fires during the copy phase or at t=0, and barely fires at t=1. About 70% of activation mass is in the original phase at t=2..7: mostly first occurrences of the input tokens y (most precise, about 0.84 at t>=2 and the strongest activations, especially on repeated y y), s, v and l, with weaker firing on x/d/q. About 30% is at the <DEL> step, where the firing rate drops steeply with sequence length (about 45% for L=3..5, 26% for L=6, near 0 for L>=8). The activation also rises when the first token is o/f/j/z/p. Precision is only about 0.5 because the same tokens and delimiters often do not fire, so magnitude seems to depend on hidden-state context that these variables do not capture. It does not fire on repeated tokens (in_first=0 rate 0.8%) or on most other letters and digits.
